name: project-memory
description: A free plugin for Claude Code. After every reply it keeps a journal of your work and a note of where you stopped, so the next conversation starts where the last one ended, and every change to your notes is kept. Everything stays on your computer.
description_good_justification: The README's first lines and the project page say what it does and what problem it solves: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory#readme
interact_justification: The README says how to install it, use it and get help; questions go to GitHub Discussions and problems to issues: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SUPPORT.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says what a change needs (a test that fails first, node check.mjs passing) and the pull-request template repeats it: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#sending-a-change
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers install, use, privacy, updating and removing it; docs/how-it-works.md explains every part: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/docs/how-it-works.md
documentation_interface_justification: Users ask in their own words; the README's 'Using it' table shows what each request does. The commands behind it (search, show, history, restore, forget, promote, status, doctor) are documented in skills/memory/SKILL.md, and the files it writes in PRIVACY.md and docs/how-it-works.md.
sites_https_justification: The repository (github.com) and the project page (zdraveski.github.io) are served only over HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and Discussions: searchable, each message has a URL, and new people can join without proprietary software: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/discussions
english_justification: All documentation is in English, and reports in English are accepted.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: frequent releases (v1.0.0 to v1.3.0), with the tests running on every change.
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when.
repo_interim_justification: Every commit between releases is public on master, and the tests run on each one.
version_unique_justification: Each release has its own version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json and its own tag.
version_tags_justification: Every release is tagged (v1.0.0 to v1.3.0): https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/tags
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md, written for users, and the same notes on each GitHub release: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: Privacy and security fixes are listed in each release's notes (from 1.2.3 under their own 'Privacy' heading). None has had a CVE.
report_process_justification: GitHub issues with a bug template; SUPPORT.md says where to report what: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: No bug reports have been filed by others yet; reports go to the GitHub issue tracker and get an answer.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests have been filed by others yet; the 'idea' issue template and Discussions take them.
report_archive_justification: Issues and Discussions are public and searchable on GitHub: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/issues
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md asks for private reports through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports in the last 6 months; SECURITY.md promises an answer within a week.
build_justification: Nothing to build: plain JavaScript (ES modules) run directly by Node.js, with no compile or bundle step.
test_justification: Six test suites, each run with one node command (listed in CONTRIBUTING.md); GitHub Actions runs `node check.mjs` and all six on Windows, macOS and Linux: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
test_invocation_justification: The tests run with documented commands, one `node <name>.test.mjs` per suite (CONTRIBUTING.md); there is no package.json (the project has no dependencies), so `npm test` is not used.
test_most_justification: Six test suites cover the rules, and CI runs them on every pull request. At the last full mutation run (v1.2.7) they caught more than 3,000 planted bugs, apart from the ones listed in automut-ignore.txt with a reason (mutate.mjs). That run is no longer part of a release.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the tests on every pull request and every push to master: Linux on Node.js 22, Windows on 24 and macOS on 26 (.github/workflows/test.yml).
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: 'Add or update a test with every change to what the plugin does' and 'Write the test first and watch it fail on the old code': https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changing-the-code
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes each add a test that failed first, for example the fixes in 1.2.3 (see the commits touching *.test.mjs).
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull-request template ('A test fails without this change and passes with it').
warnings_justification: All code is ES modules, which always run in JavaScript's strict mode; `node check.mjs` also fails on unused imports and on files that don't parse; CodeQL runs weekly.
warnings_fixed_justification: check.mjs must pass before a change is pushed, and CodeQL alerts are fixed or dismissed with a reason.
warnings_strict_justification: Strict mode is always on and check.mjs is strict about what it checks, but no separate linter is run at its strictest settings.
know_secure_design_justification: The design keeps the attack surface small: no network connections, no dependencies, data only in the user's own folder, secrets redacted before anything is saved, private tags honoured, and a written privacy policy (PRIVACY.md) whose main promise, that private text is never saved, the fuzzer checks after every round.
know_common_errors_justification: The tests and the fuzzer target the errors common to this kind of software: secrets leaking into saved text, two processes writing at once, half-written files, killed processes, disk errors and time-zone mistakes.
crypto_published_justification: No security function relies on cryptography: it makes no network connections and stores plain files locally. SHA-256 from Node.js is used only to fingerprint files.
crypto_call_justification: No cryptography is implemented; Node.js's built-in SHA-256 is called only to fingerprint files.
crypto_floss_justification: No security function relies on cryptography.
crypto_working_justification: No security function relies on cryptography.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No security function relies on cryptography.
crypto_random_justification: It generates no keys or nonces.
delivery_mitm_justification: It is installed by Claude Code's /plugin command from GitHub over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are fetched over HTTP; installation is a git fetch over HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known vulnerability has been left unfixed for more than 60 days.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Privacy and security fixes are released as soon as their tests pass (for example 1.2.3).
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository holds no credentials; the tests use made-up secret shapes only.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (JavaScript and GitHub Actions) runs weekly: .github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's JavaScript queries look for common vulnerabilities such as injection and unsafe paths.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL alerts are fixed or dismissed with a written reason; none is open in the plugin's own code.
dynamic_analysis_justification: A fuzzer (fuzz.mjs) exists and runs by hand for a bug hunt: random conversations, time-zone changes, disk errors and killed runs, checking after every round that no note loses text and nothing private is saved. Since 2026-11-09 a release does not require it.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzzer checks its invariants after every round and stops with a replayable seed on the first failure.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Fuzzer findings, when a run is made, are fixed with a test before the next release.
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The only member with access, the maintainer (zdraveski), signs in to GitHub with two-factor authentication, and GitHub asks for it again before sensitive actions such as changing settings: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md#members-with-access-to-sensitive-resources
osps_ac_02_01_justification: GitHub gives a collaborator no access until the owner invites them by hand. GOVERNANCE.md requires a review first and the least access that does the job; there is no collaborator besides the owner: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md#granting-access
osps_ac_03_01_justification: master's GitHub ruleset blocks direct pushes: every change comes through a pull request that passes the required checks, and nobody, the maintainer included, can bypass it: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md#changes-reach-master-only-through-a-pull-request
osps_ac_03_02_justification: master's ruleset forbids deleting it and force-pushing to it, with no bypass: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md#changes-reach-master-only-through-a-pull-request
osps_br_01_01_justification: Untrusted values (a pull request's SHAs, a push's previous SHA, a release's tag) reach run: scripts only through env:, never as an expression inside the script, and are checked first: the sign-off check takes only 40-hex SHAs, the release only a vX.Y.Z tag. No workflow uses branch names, titles or commit messages: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/.github/workflows/dco.yml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull requests run on pull_request only (no pull_request_target or workflow_run), so a fork's code gets no secrets and a read-only token; checkouts keep no credentials; the project keeps no secrets at all: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/.github/workflows/test.yml
osps_br_03_01_justification: The project's channels are github.com (code, issues, Discussions, releases) and zdraveski.github.io (project page, HTTPS enforced), served only over HTTPS: https://zdraveski.github.io/project-memory/
osps_br_03_02_justification: Claude Code installs the plugin from GitHub with git over HTTPS; release files are served by GitHub over HTTPS, with SHA-256 hashes and a signed attestation: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release
osps_br_07_01_justification: The project keeps no secrets, and GitHub secret scanning and push protection are on: a push holding a known kind of secret is refused: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#secrets
osps_do_01_01_justification: The README covers installing, every request and command, privacy, updating and removing it; forget, the one destructive command, lists first and removes only what you confirm: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/README.md#using-it
osps_do_02_01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the README say to run the doctor check, then open an issue with the bug template; security problems are reported privately: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SUPPORT.md
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Public GitHub Discussions for questions and ideas, issues for problems and proposals, and pull requests for changes: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/discussions
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to contribute, from running the tests to opening a pull request: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#sending-a-change
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released files are the source itself, under the same MIT license: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/LICENSE
osps_le_03_01_justification: The LICENSE file at the repository's root: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: Each release's .tar.gz and .zip is a git archive of its tag and holds LICENSE, and an install with /plugin gets the repository, LICENSE included: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/.github/workflows/release.yml
osps_qa_01_01_justification: Public on GitHub at a fixed address: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory
osps_qa_01_02_justification: The public git history records each change, its author and its time, and master can't be force-pushed: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/commits/master
osps_qa_02_01_justification: The plugin has no dependencies: it uses only Node.js's built-in modules, so there is no package.json or other list to keep: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_qa_04_01_justification: One repository holds the whole project: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory
osps_qa_05_01_justification: The repository holds only source (JavaScript, Markdown, JSON, YAML, HTML and CSS) and the documentation's images; nothing generated or executable: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only binary files are the documentation's images (PNG and WebP in docs/); no executables or libraries: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/tree/master/docs
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact (the maintainer, zdraveski) and links the private reporting form: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-problem
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The repository's default token permission for workflows is read-only, and every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top; a job gets more only by naming it: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/tree/master/.github/workflows
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has its own semantic version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json and its own tag, vX.Y.Z: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/tags
osps_br_04_01_justification: CHANGELOG.md describes each release's changes for users, with privacy and security fixes under their own heading, and each GitHub release carries the same notes: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: The plugin has no dependencies, so the release pipeline ingests no packages; its only inputs are GitHub Actions, fetched by the Actions runner at pinned commit SHAs and kept current by Dependabot: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_br_06_01_justification: From 1.2.4, the release workflow attaches SHA256SUMS for the release's archives and a Sigstore-signed build-provenance attestation of all three files (actions/attest-build-provenance): https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/.github/workflows/release.yml
osps_do_06_01_justification: SECURITY.md says the plugin takes no dependencies, and how the CI's actions are chosen, pinned by SHA and updated by Dependabot: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_do_07_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: no build step, Node.js 22 or newer and git, how to get the code and run the tests: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#running-from-source
osps_gv_01_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists everyone with access to sensitive resources: the sole maintainer, zdraveski: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md#members-with-access-to-sensitive-resources
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes what the maintainer, contributors and security reporters each do: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md sets what a change needs: a test that fails first, node check.mjs passing, a changelog line, signed-off commits and the required checks: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changing-the-code
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit in a pull request must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off matching its author; the dco workflow checks it, and it is a required check on master: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
osps_qa_03_01_justification: master's ruleset lets a pull request merge only when its required checks pass (the tests on three systems and dco), with no bypass: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md#changes-reach-master-only-through-a-pull-request
osps_qa_06_01_justification: test.yml runs check.mjs and the six test suites on every pull request, on Linux, macOS and Windows, and its jobs must pass to merge: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
osps_sa_01_01_justification: The security assessment lists every actor (the user, Claude Code, Claude, the three hooks, the memory tool, git, other processes, the maintainer and GitHub) and what each does; how-it-works.md shows when each runs: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/docs/security-assessment.md#actors-and-actions
osps_sa_02_01_justification: Every external interface: the hook events with their payload fields and outputs, the transcripts, the files written, the environment variables, git and the memory tool's commands, with links to the details: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/docs/security-assessment.md#external-interfaces
osps_sa_03_01_justification: The security assessment weighs the likely and high-impact problems (secrets saved, private text leaking, concurrent writes, a malicious transcript, a destructive command, a broken hook, the supply chain) and what guards against each: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/docs/security-assessment.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md: an answer within a week, a fix within 30 days of confirming the problem, a GitHub advisory once it is fixed, and 90 days before a reporter publishes: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#how-a-report-is-handled
osps_vm_03_01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is on, and SECURITY.md links its form: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: A fixed vulnerability is published as a GitHub security advisory, with the affected versions and what to do, and in CHANGELOG.md under the version that fixes it: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#how-a-report-is-handled
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow reads only, and only the jobs that need more get it: CodeQL and Scorecard security-events: write (Scorecard also id-token: write, for its badge), and the release job contents: write, id-token: write and attestations: write: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/tree/master/.github/workflows
osps_br_01_04_justification: The hand-started workflows take their inputs through env: and turn them into a number from 1 to 256 before use (fuzz.yml, .github/plan-mutants.mjs); the mutate shard reaches its script through env:; the release tag must match vX.Y.Z: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
osps_br_02_02_justification: From 1.2.4, each release file is named with the release's tag (project-memory-<tag>.tar.gz and .zip), SHA256SUMS lists them by name, and the attestation ties each to the tag's commit: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release
osps_br_07_02_justification: SECURITY.md's secrets policy: none are kept; only GitHub's per-job token is used; how a secret would be stored, who could read it, when it is rotated, and what to do if one leaks: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#secrets
osps_do_03_01_justification: SECURITY.md: check the files with sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS and gh attestation verify, and the output to expect: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release
osps_do_03_02_justification: SECURITY.md names the expected signer, the release workflow (certificate identity https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/<tag>, issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com), checked with gh attestation verify --signer-workflow: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release
osps_do_04_01_justification: Only the latest release gets fixes, bug and security fixes alike, until the next release; no older branches are kept up to date: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_05_01_justification: A version stops getting security updates the day the next one is released: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_gv_04_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md: nobody gets write, maintainer or admin access, or a secret, before the maintainer has reviewed their record and identity and recorded the grant: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md#granting-access
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Nothing is compiled: the released files are the JavaScript source, run as is by Node.js, with no dependencies: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#running-from-source
osps_qa_04_02_justification: One repository holds the whole project; there are no subprojects: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory
osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says how to run each suite, what it tests and how to read its result, and that CI runs them on every pull request and every push to master: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
osps_qa_06_03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: every change to what the plugin does adds or updates a test, written first and seen to fail, and a change without one isn't merged: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changing-the-code
osps_qa_07_01_justification: One maintainer and no second human reviewer, so master's ruleset requires no approval. Each change is reviewed from its diff alone before it merges, often by an AI agent, which is not a human approval: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/GOVERNANCE.md#changes-reach-master-only-through-a-pull-request
osps_sa_03_02_justification: The threat model sets out the trust boundaries, the interfaces an attacker can reach and each threat to the critical paths (redaction, private tags, the store's lock and checked writes, path checks, git calls, the supply chain), with its guard and what remains: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/docs/security-assessment.md#trust-boundaries
osps_vm_04_02_justification: No third-party component ships (the plugin has no dependencies), so there is no vulnerability in one to declare not exploitable; SECURITY.md says a VEX statement will be published if one ever ships: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_01_justification: Since 2026-11-09 no time limit is set for dependency findings: the plugin ships no dependencies, and Dependabot alerts can only concern the CI's actions. A license must be OSI-approved: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_02_justification: Since 2026-11-09 an open Dependabot alert does not hold up a release; the plugin ships no dependencies: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#releasing
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Dependency review was removed on 2026-11-09: the plugin ships no dependencies, and nothing blocks a pull request on one. Dependabot still raises alerts on the pinned CI actions.
osps_vm_06_01_justification: Since 2026-11-09 CodeQL alerts block neither a merge nor a release; they are fixed or dismissed with a written reason as the maintainer gets to them: https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/SECURITY.md#code-scanning
osps_vm_06_02_justification: CodeQL scans master weekly and blocks nothing; changes are not evaluated one by one (since 2026-11-09): https://github.com/zdraveski/project-memory/blob/master/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
